audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is called a blind in four places ('blind your autos', 'the blind does not stop Q damage'). It is not a blind. Quickdraw is also described as a two-charge ability throughout ('two Quickdraw charges', 'bait his Quickdraw charges first — once both are spent'). It is a single-cast cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen: 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' Sight reduction and an impact slow — no blind. Riot's text for Quickdraw gives one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s, with 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill'. The page's advice to 'wait until both charges are spent' describes a resource Graves does not have, and it inverts the real counterplay: keep him off basic attacks and the single dash stays on its full 16 seconds.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts your sight and slows on impact; it does not blind. Quickdraw is one dash on 16 to 12s, and its cooldown only drops when he lands basic attacks — deny the autos and you deny the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is untimed. Quickdraw, Smoke Screen and Collateral Damage are all named as spikes with no cooldown attached.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16 down to 12s, Smoke Screen 26 down to 18s, End of the Line 13 down to 6s, Collateral Damage 100/80/60s. Smoke Screen at 26 seconds is the longest basic cooldown in the lane by a distance and the page treats it as a constant threat rather than a resource he spends.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1 — once he spends it, you have nearly half a minute of clean vision. Quickdraw 16 to 12s. Collateral Damage 100 to 60s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are entirely absent. (a) New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units, so minions physically block his shells. (b) End of the Line detonates after 1 second OR on colliding with terrain, so a wall makes it explode instantly.
audit.why: Both come straight from Riot's descriptions and both change where a Rumble stands. Keeping the wave between you means his shotgun spread lands on minions instead of you, which is the single cheapest defence in the matchup and appears nowhere. And the shell's fuse is your reaction window — in the open you get a full second to walk off it, but fight him against the wall and it detonates the moment it clips terrain. _missing-interactions flags terrain-cuts-retreat for End of the Line and is correct.
audit.corrected: New Destiny's 4 bullets cannot pass through units — stand behind your wave and the spread eats minions. End of the Line fuses for 1 second in the open but detonates on contact with terrain, so never trade against a wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text says 'Force short trades only when his Scrap Shield is on cooldown'. Scrap Shield is Rumble's own W — Graves does not have it.
audit.why: A straightforward wrong-champion error that makes the sentence unfollowable. Replaced with the cooldown that actually gates his trade, Quickdraw at 16 to 12s, plus the fact that his autos are what shorten it.
audit.corrected: Force short trades when Quickdraw is spent, and keep him off basic attacks so it does not come back early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The wave-management block is generic and never uses the one wave fact that matters here.
audit.why: Because his bullets cannot pass through units, the wave is not just a zoning tool in this lane, it is armour. Holding the wave between you is both the standard Rumble freeze and a hard reduction in his damage output, and that overlap deserves to be stated once.
audit.corrected: Best wave keeps minions between you — his 4 bullets stop on the first unit they hit.

edits.after: Graves owns this stretch, but one fact blunts it: New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units, so keeping a minion between you eats most of a shell dump. At level 1 neither side commits. The instant he hits 2 and gets Quickdraw he dashes to minimum range where your cone barely clips him and dumps the point-blank spread. Smoke Screen is not a blind — it reduces your sight range and slows you on the initial impact — so what it really costs you is the ability to see and reposition to keep him inside the cone. It is 26 seconds at rank 1, the longest basic cooldown in the lane, so treat it as something he spends. Pre-stack Heat before any trade, and pop Scrap Shield at the start of his burst: shields eat the first pellets, not the last. Never trade with your back to a wall — End of the Line detonates on contact with terrain instead of fusing.
edits.before: Graves owns this stretch. At level 1 neither side is committed — his one ability and your Flamespitter-with-no-Heat means it is roughly even, but the instant he hits 2 and gets Quickdraw he can E to minimum range, where your Flamespitter cone barely clips him, drop Smoke Screen to blind your autos and cut your vision so your Danger Zone tracking falls apart, and dump the point-blank shell spread before your Heat builds into the empowered ticks. Try to pre-stack Heat in the wave before any trade so your Q is already powered when he dashes in, and use Scrap Shield at the start of his burst rather than waiting — shields eat the first pellets, not the last. His Smoke Screen is your biggest problem: you rely on your Flamespitter's sustained ticks to win trades, and the blind does not stop Q damage but it does stop you from repositioning to keep him inside the cone.

edits.after: True Grit keeps stacking armor and MR against your magic damage, and it stacks double whenever he dashes toward you. Quickdraw is one dash on 16 seconds falling to 12, not a pair of charges — and it only comes back faster when he lands basic attacks, so kiting him off his autos keeps the dash expensive for the whole trade. Force short trades once it is spent and your Heat is already near 50. At level 6, do not stand in your own Equalizer carpet expecting to burn him down inside it; he answers with Collateral Damage into a point-blank shell and a squishy Rumble folds first. Equalizer is worth more as a zone tool at river and objectives. Fight in the open, never against a wall, because End of the Line detonates the moment it touches terrain instead of giving you its one-second fuse.
edits.before: Graves' True Grit keeps stacking armor and MR into your magic damage across the entire mid-game, and his two Quickdraw charges mean every time you land an Electro-Harpoon slow he can E-dash out before your Danger Zone Q finishes cooking. At level 6, do not stand inside your own Equalizer carpet expecting to Flamespitter him down inside it — he fires Collateral Damage into auto into Q point-blank and a squishy Rumble folds faster than the carpet damages him. Equalizer is most valuable here as a zone tool at river and objectives, not as a duel button in lane. Force short trades only when his Scrap Shield is on cooldown and your Heat is already near 50; never brawl extended fights where True Grit stacking and double E charges beat your frontloaded AP damage.

notes: Four errors corrected. (1) Smoke Screen was called a blind in four places — Riot's text has it reducing sight range and slowing on the initial impact, with no blind at all; the practical cost to Rumble is losing the repositioning that keeps Graves in the cone, not losing autos. (2) Quickdraw was described throughout as a two-charge ability; it is one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s whose cooldown drops when he lands basic attacks, which inverts the counterplay to 'deny his autos'. (3) The mid text told the player to 'force short trades when his Scrap Shield is on cooldown' — Scrap Shield is Rumble's own W, not a Graves ability. (4) Two decisive interactions were missing: New Destiny's 4 bullets cannot pass through units, making the wave real mitigation, and End of the Line detonates on contact with terrain rather than fusing for its full second, so trading against a wall removes your reaction window. The Graves entry in _missing-interactions ('terrain-cuts-retreat, End of the Line') is a real interaction and is now on the page.
